articleTitle: On Different Methods For Automated MILP Solver Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: In this paper we review models, methods and ideas all intended to improve performance of mixed integer programming (MIP) solvers, such as Gurobi. Aside from task instances as an input, MIP solvers also receive a set of tunable parameters that affect the performance of a solver. Successful parameter configuration may lead to the solver’s performance increase, but such configurations usually work fine only for specific task family, so for different tasks new configuration must be found. The number of parameters in such configurations varies with each different solver, but it may vary from 20 to 100, which makes the solver’s parameter configuration difficult and time-consuming, as you need to test a specific task set on each configuration. That’s why, in this paper we discuss different ways to automatize configuration process, and also suggest a way to improve its efficiency.Base tasks we use for benchmark are instances of multicore processor scheduling problem. For automated parameter configuration we use variable neighborhood search (VNS) [1]. To optimize configuration process we suggest to use large language models (LLM) to obtain same-size embeddings (vector representations of tasks), even for instances with different dimensionalities, so we could use them to train linear regression model to predict parameters of solver for each particular instance without running VNS on them.

articleTitle: The Comprehensive Deep Learning Models for Phishing Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Internet technologies develop very fast today. It resulted in essential growth in different types of cyberattacks and cyberthreats. Cybercriminals are becoming more advanced and utilize various techniques to access users’ confidential and financial data, avoiding their defense systems. Among these types of attacks, phishing attacks are among the most dangerous as they lead users to malicious websites where criminals can easily steal their data and credentials. Although traditional defense methods allow protection from some of these threats, they are becoming less effective due to the development of the Artificial Intelligence field. Three types of neural networks, including convolutional, recurrent, and a combination of convolutional and recurrent neural networks, were applied for protection against phishing. In the experimental results, the dataset of 392924 legitimate and 146422 malicious URLs has been used. These neural networks have received accuracy scores of 0.613, 0.719, and 0.841. The combined model showed the best scores among all models.

articleTitle: WRDScore: New Metric for Evaluation of Natural Language Generation Models
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: Evaluating natural language generation models, particularly for method name prediction, poses significant challenges. A robust metric must account for the versatility of method naming, considering both semantic and syntactic variations. Traditional overlap-based metrics, such as ROUGE, fail to capture these nuances. Existing embedding-based metrics often suffer from imbalanced precision and recall, lack normalized scores, or make unrealistic assumptions about sequences. To address these limitations, we leverage the theory of optimal transport and construct WRDScore, a novel metric that strikes a balance between simplicity and effectiveness. In the WRDScore framework, we define precision as the maximum degree to which the predicted sequence’s tokens are included in the reference sequence, token by token. Recall is calculated as the total cost of the optimal transport plan that maps the reference sequence to the predicted one. Finally, WRDScore is computed as the harmonic mean of precision and recall, balancing these two complementary metrics. Our metric is lightweight, normalized, and precision-recall-oriented, avoiding unrealistic assumptions while aligning well with human judgments. Experiments on a human-curated dataset confirm the superiority of WRDScore over other available text metrics.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Distance Measures for Unsupervised Speaker Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of various distance measures for unsupervised speaker change detection (SCD) using Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), which capture essential characteristics of the speech signal. The study identifies the most effective distance metrics and thresholds for achieving high F1 scores by optimizing each distance measure for its respective threshold. Experiments were conducted using multiple distance metrics, including Euclidean distance, cosine similarity, Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, vector quantization (VQ) distortion, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, and others. Among them, VQ distortion and Bray-Curtis dissimilarity achieved the highest F1 scores of 89.21 and 89.29, respectively, while Euclidean distance showed comparable results with an F1 score of 89.15. Precision, recall, and accuracy were used as key metrics to assess the performance of each distance measure. The study underscores the importance of selecting suitable distance measures and thresholds to balance precision, recall, and accuracy in SCD systems, enhancing their robustness and reliability in practical applications. These results contribute to the development of more effective methods for speaker change detection.

articleTitle: Dynamic Optimization of Minimum Document Frequency for Extractive Text Summarization Using GreedSum Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This research presents a significant advancement in the GreedSum algorithm, a previously introduced extractive text summarization method. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the minimum document frequency (mindf) parameter within the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) framework. By integrating a clustering approach, we explored the hypothesis that optimizing the min-df for individual documents can enhance the quality of summaries, as measured by ROUGE scores. The methodology involved grouping similar documents into clusters and fine-tuning the min-df parameter based on cluster characteristics. Extensive experimentation with a large dataset confirmed that this dynamic optimization yields superior results compared to static parameter settings. The findings underscore a novel strategy for improving the accuracy and relevance of automated summarization in scientific literature, offering a tailored approach that adapts to the unique features of each document cluster. This research not only refines the summarization process but also opens new avenues for adaptive natural language processing systems in information extraction and text analysis. Future work will focus on refining dynamic parameter adjustment techniques and exploring additional evaluation metrics to enhance the robustness and applicability of summarization tools across various domains.

articleTitle: Stabilization the Electric Arc Plasma Flow by Its Own Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: In this work, based on the system of MHD equations, numerical studies of electric arc plasma fluxes generated by a welding plasma torch were carried out. When writing the equations, it was assumed that the flow is axisymmetric, laminar, and the plasma is optically thin. An analysis of the operation of the plasmatron depending on the strength of the electric current and the flow rate of the plasma-forming gas is made. In the course of numerical experiments, it was found that in the region of high gas flow rates, which are called marginal, there is a loss of stability of the solution of the system of equations. Such regions were found for different values of electric currents (50A, 60A, 70A and 100A) and for Ar and CO2 gases. The system of stationary MHD equations was solved both in the variables "vortex-current function" and in physical variables. The results obtained for the studied areas are identical in both cases. In our opinion, the results obtained in the course of numerical studies can be interpreted as the boundary of the application of laminar MHD equations. An analysis of experimental Schlieren interferograms of electric arc plasma flows shows that in these areas there is a transition from the laminar flow regime of electric arc plasma to a turbulent one. This suggests that the loss of stability of the solution occurs near the transition of the laminar flow regime to a turbulent one.

articleTitle: Optimization of Computations in Simulating Chemical Kinetics Using Surrogate Neural Models
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: We investigate how deep learning-based methods can be applied to solve stiff systems of ordinary differential equations modeling complex chemical kinetic systems. We use artificial neural networks (ANN) as a time-step integrator: ANN reproduces the evolution of a given chemical state for a short period of time. Thus, it can potentially replace computationally expensive stiff solvers, giving a substantial speed-up. This improvement is crucial in simulating a large number of simultaneous reactions that can happen, for example, in almost all combustion problems in aircraft and rocket jet engines, industrial installations for the pyrogenic synthesis of nanomaterials, processes in chemical and technological industrial installations, for example, in chemical reactors. In order to achieve an acceptable improvement in inference time while maintaining prediction accuracy, different techniques are applied to help ANNs assimilate chemical system structure: clustering of phase space and auto-regression. The last one is enhanced with curriculum learning methods. The described approach is tested on a basic Robertson problem. The approach may be promising to further speed up of numerical modeling while maintaining acceptable accuracy of ODE solution.

articleTitle: Hybrid QKD Approach for Multi-User Quantum Networks: Practical Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: As concerns about the robustness of current security solutions against quantum-based attacks continue to escalate, the limitations of existing Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols, which are predominantly designed for point-to-point communication scenarios, become increasingly apparent. This paper addresses these limitations by conducting a comprehensive analysis of contemporary twin-field-based algorithms, examining their individual characteristics and overall performance metrics. By synthesizing insights from Twin-Field QKD protocols, cutting-edge advancements in Quantum Communication technologies, and well-established point-to-point solutions, a novel network-oriented concept for a Hybrid Twin-Field QKD protocol is proposed. This innovative approach aims to facilitate secure quantum communication among multiple users within a network, offering a practical and resource-efficient alternative to traditional point-to-point methods. The proposed Hybrid Twin-Field QKD protocol seeks to address the need for scalable and robust security solutions in the face of evolving quantum threats, thereby enhancing the effectiveness, applicability, and efficiency of quantum key distribution systems in multi-user network environments.

articleTitle: Optimization of Database Operations in the Application for Text Corpus Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: The user's comfortable work with large volumes of text is ensured by optimizing the web application. This optimization is primarily focused on optimizing work with the database. The SQL query language is an example of a declarative language that allows for effective query optimization.The article formalizes the optimization problem as improving the quality of application usage by increasing the user's productivity in the system. This is achieved by reducing the reaction time of the system in response to user actions.There are three main strategies for query optimization: modifying the source code of the program that interacts with the database, modifying the structure of queries, and modifying the structure of the database itself. The technologies used to create the optimized software system include: the application was written in Python using the Flask web framework. Work with the database was done using the SQLAlchemy library and PostgreSQL was chosen as the DBMS (Database Management System). To test the functionality of the optimized queries, the pytest library was used.Specific optimization examples were presented for the following situations: long execution time for any stage of a data request can be solved by changing the query structure by adding an index. Long execution time for any stage of data change can be solved by deleting the index from the query. A large number of queries within a cycle can be replaced with an equivalent query outside the loop to improve performance.The results of the computational experiments demonstrate the high efficiency of the optimization technique.

articleTitle: On Simulation Inter Districts Transport Flows
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: This paper describes the functionality of the developed simulation system "Inter-district Road Traffic". The modeling of traffic flows on a city map divided into districts has been considered. To solve the problems of traffic optimization and the placement of traffic objects, a two-stage model has been selected, including the matrices of correspondence between districts and traffic distribution along the routes of the transport network. The first block of the two-stage model has been calculated numerically using the Sinkhorn algorithm. The second block has been calculated using the universal method of similar triangles. The developed modeling tool can be used to solve traffic optimization problems in an urban environment - to find optimal traffic in the city between districts, taking into account the location of houses, the intensity of flows, the distribution of flows along routes and other additional conditions. When developing the application, the open source React library has been used to create user interfaces, and D3 (an open source JavaScript library for data visualization) has been used to visualize graphs and work with data.

articleTitle: Auto-Start Solution with Neural Video Vision for Powering Up Traffic Management
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: The article discusses current R&D on the intellectualization of traffic lights equipped with IP video cameras. It shows the application areas of smart traffic lights and describes the stages of designing and semi-industrial testing of the prototype, the core of which is a Raspberry Pi 4 mini PC. During the design and construction of the hardware and software complex (HSC), features of frame-by-frame methods for webcams and streaming methods for IP video cameras for AI image recognition were identified. To increase vandal, water, and dust resistance and reliability for semi-industrial testing of the prototype, an outdoor IP video camera by HIKVISION in the EXIR Fixed Mini Bullet Network Camera modification was used. Periodic power outages at intersections in Almaty required research and development of a method for automatic start-up of the HSC from the moment of power loss. The proposed BIOS configuration algorithm for the Raspberry Pi 4 mini PC is novel and unique in its OS Raspbian settings as a non-standard version of Debian GNU/Linux. The found solutions and test results demonstrated the reliability of the automatic start-up of the traffic light with neural computer vision. Smart traffic lights with video vision allow adaptive control of traffic lights with AI in street conditions at the Abay/Saina interchange in the metropolis of Almaty.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Traffic Management for Busy Intersections
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: A modern system of intelligent dispatching for a complex road infrastructure facility in the metropolis of Almaty is being presented. To improve the existing automated traffic management system (ATMS) in the city and to gradually implement digital traffic technologies with autopilot vehicles, a crucial and pressing task for IT is to replace the traffic police dispatcher-employee with a neural network-based artificial intelligence. The work demonstrates the methods and results of implementing a neural network into a mobile server program for the AnyLogic environment using the SUMO application. This approach, using the built-in TraCI connector, established connections with Python scripts of the server program AnylogicRaspberryServer.py. Testing and analysis of the research results showed the adequacy of virtual dispatching, which allowed reducing the load on the traffic police employee under moderate and average traffic conditions. It is noted that manual control of the situation at the Abay/Saina intersection is more preferable during peak hours. The obtained software products and the semi-industrial prototype of the local ISU with AI are protected by copyright certificates and have important practical significance.

articleTitle: Centerless Quantum Key Distribution Protocol based on Superposition
publicationTitle: 2024 20th International Asian School-Seminar on Optimization Problems of Complex Systems (OPCS)
abstract: In today's digital age, where cyber threats are escalating and data security is paramount, traditional cryptographic methods face significant challenges. Classic security systems, such as Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and SSL/TLS protocols, rely heavily on asymmetric cryptography to protect sensitive information. However, with the exponential growth of data and advancements in quantum computing, there is an increasing need for more robust encryption methods. This paper introduces a new decentralized multi-user quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol based on quantum superposition, which aims to address the limitations of current cryptographic systems. The protocol leverages quantum principles to enhance the security and efficiency of data transmission, overcoming the vulnerabilities exposed by potential quantum computing threats. The methodology of implementing this protocol, including the setup of quantum sources, detectors, and optical components, as well as the integration with classical communication channels are presented. The results demonstrate that the proposed QKD protocol not only achieves high accuracy and reliability but also scales effectively in network environments.
